prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics, especially from the preceding modules Mechanics 1, Mechanics 2 and Mechanics 3.
Successful completion of StEOP (Study Introduction and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: Describe and explain basic concepts of selected topics in strength of materials in a structured manner.
Explain and perform calculations in tensor notation.
Specify and explain Saint-Venant's problems of prismatic bars and their general solution.
Solve problems of torsion, transverse force bending, and warping torsion for thin-walled cross-section bars.
Identify problems of planar surface structures (discs and plates) and solve them for rotationally symmetric cases.
Explain the Ritz and Galerkin approximation methods and apply them to problems of beam and plate bending.
Categorize problems of spatial surface structures (shells).
Analyze complex problems in a structured manner.
Systematically validate results using analytical and numerical benchmarks.
Implement solution approaches in a targeted manner.

syllabus_topics: Torsion of straight bars with arbitrary cross-sections (thin-walled cross-sections, shear center, warping torsion)
Thin-walled surface structures (plates and shells); specific example problems for rotationally symmetric problems
